title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's preparatory notes for his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (pd) de Rham complex. Notation, inferred from context:
- S is a ring with a pd ideal S^+ and an element t ∈ S^+.
- A_*(S,S^+,t) is a simplicial commutative differential graded algebra. In degree n it is the pd de Rham complex of the 'simplex of size t':
  A_n = S{X_0,…,X_n}[dX_0,…,dX_n] / (ΣX_i − t, ΣdX_i)_pd.
- S{…} denotes the divided-power polynomial algebra and [dX] the exterior algebra on the dX_i.
- Face and degeneracy maps are the usual simplicial ones on the barycentric coordinates X_i.

This is a divided-power, 'parametrised' version of Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial forms ∇(n,*) = Q[t_0..t_n, dt_0..dt_n]/(Σt_i − 1, Σdt_i). Two things change: polynomials become pd polynomials, and the constraint Σt_i = 1 becomes Σ X_i = t with t a pd element.

The universal case is S = k{T}, S^+ = its augmentation ideal, t = T. This gives the simplicial dg k-algebra A_{k*}.

What the page does.
1. It announces the study of the automorphisms of A_{k*}. It notes that clean results appear only after completion, giving Â_{k*}.
2. It computes the completed terms:
   Â_{k,n} ≅ k{{X_0..X_n}}[dX_0..dX_n]/(ΣdX_i).
   Here T is recovered as ΣX_i. Equivalently,
   Â_{k,n} ≅ k{{T}}{{X_0..X_n}}[dX]/(ΣX_i − T, ΣdX_i)_pd ≅ k{{T}}{{X_0..X_{n−1}}}[dX_0..dX_{n−1}].
   The last step is the pd change of variable X_n ↦ X_n + ΣX_i − T. It is legitimate precisely because T lies in a pd ideal, so (T − ΣX_i)^{[m]} makes sense.
3. It states that results on lifting or extending maps (Â_{k,n} into some Â_{k',n}) are the same as in the general completed case A_*(S,S^+,t)^∧ with S ≅ k{{T}}. In that case
   A_n(S,S^+,t)^∧ ≅ S{{X_0..X_n}}[dX]/(ΣX_i − t, ΣdX_i)_pd ≅ S{{X_0..X_{n−1}}}[dX_0..dX_{n−1}].
4. One caveat is noted. Certain auxiliary elements A'_1 and B'_i (i ≥ 1), presumably introduced on earlier pages, live in A_1(S,S^+,t)^∧ ≅ S{{X_0}} rather than in S{X_0}. The pd polynomials in X_0 that expressed them therefore become pd power series. The sentence breaks off there.

Purpose. Most likely the aim is to understand the symmetry and rigidity of the universal simplicial pd de Rham algebra, and to use it in integral or characteristic-p comparisons with simplicial cochains.
errors: In the first displayed isomorphism, the relation ΣX_i = T is implicit, since T is eliminated as ΣX_i. This is consistent but written tersely.
The reduction to n−1 variables needs t ∈ S^+, i.e. t must have divided powers. This holds in the setting described.
The text is fragmentary and breaks off mid-sentence, so the claimed lifting statements cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Simplicial pd de Rham algebra of simplices A_n = S{X_0..X_n}[dX]/(ΣX_i − t, ΣdX_i)_pd, with the parameter t in a pd ideal
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra ∇(•,*) (integral/char-p cochain models)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for the rational version; Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for the simplicial formalism; pd/integral variants appear in scattered later work
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; a 1976 IHÉS lecture, no written version known to me

ideas.what: Computation of the completed terms as pd power series over k{{T}} in n variables, tensored with an exterior algebra
ideas.modern_name: pd change of variables / pd Poincaré-type structure of the completed simplex

ideas.what: Programme to determine the automorphisms of the universal simplicial pd dg-algebra A_*(k{T}, k{T}^+, T), after completion
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms / symmetries of simplicial cochain-algebra models

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to compute the automorphism group of the universal simplicial pd de Rham algebra A_*(k{T}, k{T}^+, T), with the 'simplex size' T a pd variable, after completing it. He also notes that the auxiliary elements A'_1 and B'_i become pd power series rather than pd polynomials. Neither this automorphism computation nor the parametrised (Σx_i = t) pd Sullivan algebra appears in the literature to my knowledge.
missed.quote: Nous nous intéressons maintenant aux automorphismes de la k-algèbre différentielle simpliciale A_{k*} = A_*(k{T}, k{T}^+, T). Mais on trouve des résultats simples qu'en complétant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: pd/integral versions of Sullivan's forms are relevant to integral and p-adic homotopy theory and to comparisons between crystalline and Betti cochains. An analysis of their symmetries, especially with a pd 'size' parameter, could bear on functoriality questions in these models.

missed.claim: The page links crystalline divided-power techniques to Sullivan-type simplicial de Rham models of homotopy types, around 1976, contemporaneous with Sullivan's work.
missed.quote: A_n(S,S^+,t)^∧ ≃ S{{X_0,…,X_n}}[dX_0,…,dX_n] mod idéal à p.d. engendré par ΣX_i − t, ΣdX_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early precursor to pd/integral cochain models, an area later pursued by other means (E∞-algebras, Mandell).

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck working in 1976 with a divided-power Sullivan-type simplicial de Rham algebra carrying a pd size parameter T, and planning to study its automorphisms. This is notable as unpublished context, but the page itself is mostly routine pd computations and the thread is cut off.
transcription_corrections: The second isomorphism should read k{{T}}{{X_0,…,X_n}}[dX_0,…,dX_n]/(ΣX_i − T, ΣdX_i)_pd; the subscript 'pd' marks the ideal as a pd ideal.
The illegible parenthesis reads approximately '(où on prend pour S ≃ k{{T}})'; the struck-through word is crossed out in the manuscript.
'S{{X_0,…X_{n-1}}}' in the manuscript is written with a dash: 'S{{X_0, — X_{n−1}}}'.
Handwritten page number in the margin is 173.
